subject: Post-demo prompt dossier & redaction checklist — next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@litigaze.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo prompt dossier & redaction checklist — next steps

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our side: the demo covered intent classification + clause extraction flows and we identified three priority use cases for the pilot (quick triage, auto-summarization for litigation docs, and clause-normalization for downstream search).

Next tangible asks so we can scope the eval and recommended model mix:
- A representative set of ~200 customer prompts/examples (queries + 1–3 corresponding expected outputs). Highlight any edge cases (PII, OCR artifacts, long-context threads).
- Your data schema (sample filenames and a single sample document) so we can sketch token estimates and batching impact.
- Any hard redaction/compliance constraints (PII fields to never export, retention limits).

I attached a short redaction_checklist_v1.pdf to help your team identify sensitive fields quickly. If possible, please upload the sample prompts (CSV or JSONL) and the schema to the Drive folder linked below by EOD Wednesday. Ben will pull token/latency estimates after we get the samples.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Litigaze: upload prompts + sample doc (Claire)
- Redwood: initial model recommendations + benchmark plan (Stephanie + Ben)
- Redwood: redaction guidance and mapping doc (Laura)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLitigazePromptPack
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/1142

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute sync if easier.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@litigaze.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo prompt dossier & redaction checklist — next steps

Hi Stephanie —

Appreciate the clear recap. attaching a small batch to start — see sample_prompts_batch1.jsonl (10 examples) and our data schema (litigaze_data_schema.xlsx). A few notes on the examples:
- Edge cases: OCR noise in scanned exhibits, redacted PDFs with placeholder tokens ("[REDACTED]"), and heavily formatted tables.
- PII: client SSNs and attorney emails are in the dataset; we cannot include full SSNs in the sample. We replaced these with partial tokens (e.g., "XXX-XX-1234").
- Output expectations: for clause-normalization we expect canonicalized clause names + extracted key-value pairs.

Attached: sample_prompts_batch1.jsonl (application/jsonl), litigaze_data_schema.xlsx (spreadsheet)

We can get a larger batch (~200) ready by Friday 10th. Also looping in our security contact if you need SOC2 artifacts later.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Dunn
Director of Data Product — Litigaze
claire.dunn@litigaze.com

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo prompt dossier & redaction checklist — next steps

Claire — thanks for the batch and the schema. Quick notes from an engineering/sizing perspective:
- Token estimate: based on the sample, we expect median prompt length ~420 tokens and average response length ~560 tokens for the clause-normalization task. We'll provide a cost/latency matrix for gpt-like dense models vs. our quantized Llama variants.
- Benchmarks I plan to run once we have the 200 examples: latency (p50/p95), unit cost estimate, and extraction F1 against your labeled items.
- For OCR-heavy documents, we recommend a light pre-clean step (normalize whitespace, remove page headers) — we've included a short script snippet in the Drive folder (preprocess_ocr_notes.md).

Also flagging a potential quality-regression risk: normalized clause naming is brittle to ambiguous phrasing. We'll include an eval set with adversarial prompts to track regressions during model rollouts.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Claire — great, and thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming we received the two files and the partial redactions look fine as a seed set.

1) Litigaze (Claire) — full ~200 prompt pack + 3 labeled examples per use case (due: Fri 2026-07-10)
2) Redwood (Ben + Laura) — run bench suite and return a model recommendation memo (models to evaluate, expected cost/latency, suggested quantization) + redaction mapping (due: Tue 2026-07-14)
3) Redwood (Stephanie) — coordinate pilot kickoff and a brief SOW draft for review (due: Wed 2026-07-15)

We also created a placeholder HubSpot deal (DL-2026-1142) and added the Drive link in the deal notes. If Litigaze prefers, we can send a secure upload link instead of Drive for the full dataset.

If that timeline looks good, I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute checkpoint next Monday to confirm the sample pack and labels.
